zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 5; they obstruct the view downward from Decks 5, 6, and 7, with Deck 5 having the most severe obstruction and higher decks progressively less affected, though horizon views remain clear.
zones.effect: You'll see orange boats instead of water when looking straight down, but the ocean horizon is unobstructed—matters most if you like watching the water directly below or tender operations.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who want unobstructed views straight down to the waterline; doesn't matter to those focused on horizon views or who spend little time on their balcony/at the window.

zones.what: Deck 10 overhead houses the main pool deck, buffet venue, and outdoor activity areas directly above the mid and aft sections.
zones.effect: You'll hear deck chair scraping, footfalls, and pool activity from early morning through late evening, especially in good weather when the pool deck is heavily used.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and those in cabins during the day; doesn't matter to guests who are rarely in their cabin or sleep heavily.

zones.what: Deck 9 overhead houses dining venues and public rooms in the mid and aft sections.
zones.effect: You may hear chair movement, footfalls, and activity from dining service and public room use, mostly during meal times and evening hours.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and early-to-bed guests; doesn't matter to those on a similar schedule to the venues above or who tolerate ambient noise well.

zones.what: Deck 4 below has guest cabins, but Decks 5-7 forward sit two to four decks above the main show lounge on Deck 6 and cinema on Deck 7 in the forward section.
zones.effect: The show lounge and cinema generate bass and vibration during performances and screenings, typically felt most on the deck immediately above and diminishing with distance.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests sensitive to bass and vibration during evening show times; doesn't matter to those who attend the shows anyway or who are out during performance hours.

zones.what: Primary elevator and stair banks run through the mid-ship section on all cabin decks, with machinery noise, door chimes, and passenger traffic concentrated there.
zones.effect: Cabins very close to elevators offer maximum convenience but come with mechanical hums, dings, and hallway conversation throughout the day and night; cabins farther away are quieter but require longer walks.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests prioritizing quiet over convenience, those with mobility concerns who need proximity, and families with young children making frequent cabin trips.

zones.what: These lower aft cabins sit closest to the engine room and propulsion machinery below and behind.
zones.effect: You'll experience a low-frequency hum and occasional vibration, most noticeable when the ship is at full speed or maneuvering; white noise that some find soothing and others find intrusive.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to vibration-sensitive guests and those who need absolute quiet; doesn't matter to those who sleep through white noise or find the hum comforting.

zones.what: These lower forward cabins sit above and near the bow thrusters, which activate during docking and maneuvering.
zones.effect: You'll hear and feel significant thruster noise and vibration during port arrivals and departures, typically early morning and late afternoon—brief but intense.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and early risers on port days; doesn't matter to those already awake during port operations or who sleep through mechanical noise.

zones.what: The anchor chain runs through the bow structure, closest to the lowest forward cabins.
zones.effect: When the anchor deploys or retrieves—common on tender port mornings—you'll hear loud chain rattle and grinding, typically brief but startling if unexpected.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers on itineraries with tender ports; doesn't matter on all-dock itineraries or to those already awake during tender operations.
